law: No concept may exist without ownership. No overlap may exist between constitutional domains. No cross-domain ownership permitted.
dependencyLaw: Identity -> Knowledge -> Relationships -> Context -> Policy -> Trust -> Projection. Forbidden: circular dependencies, mutual ownership, cross-domain state mutation.
communication: All cross-domain communication occurs exclusively through explicit contracts. No domain may access another domain's internals.

boundaries.projectionLaw: Products, services, offers, subscriptions, contracts are projections. No projection may own truth. Truth belongs only to constitutional domains.

categories.name: Constitution
categories.covers: The laws, amendments and certification law that govern every other category.

categories.name: Meaning
categories.covers: What exists, what it is called, and what is known about it.

categories.name: Reality and Reasoning
categories.covers: How reality is observed, evidenced, explained, simulated and changed.

categories.name: Universal Dimensions
categories.covers: The coordinates any fact is placed in: where, when, how much, what value, in which expression, in what context.

categories.name: Structure
categories.covers: How declarations are stored once and linked.

categories.name: Decision and Control
categories.covers: Who may decide, under which policy and rule, and what was decided.

categories.name: Assurance
categories.covers: Protection, computed trust, the immutable record, and obligations.

categories.name: Interaction
categories.covers: How people see, are told, converse and find.

categories.name: Automation
categories.covers: How work runs: events, state, workflows, agents and connections.

categories.name: Intelligence
categories.covers: Measurement of the platform and the business.

categories.name: Platform
categories.covers: Storing, running, verifying, holding content and offering the platform.

categories.name: Business
categories.covers: Business projections composed from the domains; they own no truth.

laws.name: Zero Hard Coding
laws.statement: Only the immutable kernel is fixed in code. No business concept — product, service, offer, subscription, contract, industry, category, brand, country, currency, language, marketplace, store, tenant, organisation, person — is modelled as a primitive or a schema type; each is a projection of primitives, and the projection changes as context changes.

laws.name: Knowledge Once
laws.statement: Every concept, fact and capability is defined once, in one canonical source, with one owner. There are no parallel definitions, no conflicting truth, no orphans, and every code module has one home.

laws.name: Projection Law
laws.statement: Truth lives in the registry. Documents, business objects and reality are projections derived from it, never authored and never a second source; everything that can be derived is derived, not stored.

laws.name: Constitutional Governance
laws.statement: Every capability, change, evolution and autonomous action is governed; no execution bypasses governance.

laws.name: Explainability
laws.statement: Every action answers what happened, why, who authorised it, which policy allowed it, what evidence supports it, what confidence exists and what alternatives were evaluated.

laws.name: Configuration Over Code
laws.statement: Behaviour is driven by metadata, ontologies, policies, rules, registries and configuration, never by product-specific code. Launching anywhere, extending or changing the platform is configuration that a person with the manual, or an agent, can do from the console or the API.
aliases: Everything Is Configurable From The Console

laws.name: Single Ownership And Contract
laws.statement: No concept exists without an owner, no capability without a boundary, no boundary without a contract, no contract without governance; no term has two meanings, no meaning two definitions, and no two domains overlap.

laws.name: Independent Authorities
laws.statement: No entity owns another domain's concern — identity, geography, time, value, security, knowledge, intelligence, analytics or governance. It relates to them: a place stores no currency, a store stores no country.
enforcedBy: test/places.js (a place's currency and locale are settings owned by Value and Expression)

laws.name: Dependency Law
laws.statement: Dependencies run Identity → Knowledge → Relationships → Context → Policy → Trust → Projection. Circular dependencies, mutual ownership and cross-domain state mutation are forbidden.

laws.name: Runtime Responsibility
laws.statement: The constitution defines truth, domains manage truth, the runtime derives reality, agents execute reality and applications consume it.

laws.name: Architectural Freeze
laws.statement: Primitives, domain ownership, contract structure and the governance, dependency and projection models are frozen. Change happens through registries, policies, capabilities, contexts, relationships, knowledge, agents and projections, never by adding primitives, and only through a recorded amendment.

laws.name: Generated Platform
laws.statement: Everything is generated from declarations: data models, APIs, interfaces, workflows, state machines, reports, dashboards, permissions, integrations, documentation, SDKs and tests. One generated API serves everyone — the console, storefronts, apps, agents, partners — with no private back door.

laws.name: Registry First
laws.statement: Everything is discoverable: if it exists it is registered, describable and searchable.

laws.name: Infinite Extensibility
laws.statement: Every domain is complete from zero to infinite and assumes no Earth, country, calendar, value unit, language or text direction. New kinds, places, categories and domains arrive by registration and configuration, never redesign; every concept is self-governing, self-describing, self-registering, self-validating, self-certifying, composable, replaceable and independently evolvable.

laws.name: Technology Agnostic
laws.statement: Nothing depends on a vendor, database, cloud or framework; each is an adapter chosen by configuration, per domain or per tenant.

laws.name: Contextual Distribution
laws.statement: Configuring a place projects what applies there — expression, value units, tax, compliance, catalogue, pricing — inherited down the place hierarchies, for any number of places at once.

laws.name: Platform-Owned Master Data
laws.statement: Master data belongs to the platform. Platforms, tenants and modules select it through views and never copy it; a tenant extends only within its own scope.

laws.name: Selection From Owners
laws.statement: Every choice offered anywhere is a selection from the domain that owns the subject, in any combination. Constraints are declared by the entities, and every option carries a free or paid offering.

laws.name: Nothing Invented
laws.statement: Creating one thing never creates another. Anything missing shows as incomplete until a person or agent completes it; nothing is filled with a placeholder.
enforcedBy: test/places.js (no place invented above the countries)

laws.name: Rules Belong To Kinds
laws.statement: A format or validation rule belongs to the kind that needs it, never to a whole domain.
enforcedBy: lib/kernel.js (attribute values checked against the type their kind declares)

laws.name: One Kernel
laws.statement: Every domain is built on the same kernel and receives every kernel part and shared service; no domain can lack one.

laws.name: Bounded Agents
laws.statement: An agent is a party with declared permissions, scope, budget and audit; it never exceeds the person or role it acts for, and money or irreversible actions need declared approval.

laws.name: Security Floor
laws.statement: Security and compliance are on by default; a tenant or operator may tighten policy but never weaken it below the platform baseline.

laws.name: Immutable Record
laws.statement: Every change and every access to sensitive data is recorded in an append-only, hash-chained record that no one can edit.
enforcedBy: lib/kernel.js and test/kernel.js (the kernel's hash-chained event log)

laws.name: Packages Compose
laws.statement: Packages compose domains into ready-made, editable platforms; a customisation is an overlay that survives every package upgrade.

laws.name: Every Law Is Enforced
laws.statement: A law without an executable check is not finished; the register records each law's enforcement, and the count of laws not yet enforced may only fall.

kernel.name: Kinds
kernel.statement: The kinds a domain contains, each declaring its attributes, where it may sit, its validation rules, its identifier schemes and whether it carries a shape. Users add kinds.
kernel.note: kinds, typed attributes, placement rules and identifier schemes are declared and checked; validation rules beyond the value type are not yet declarable

kernel.name: Nodes
kernel.statement: The instances of every kind, with no limit on count or depth.

kernel.name: Hierarchies
kernel.statement: Named hierarchies over shared nodes; a node may sit in many, and in more than one place within one.

kernel.name: Identifiers
kernel.statement: A universal ID for every node, plus any number of code schemes, declared as data.

kernel.name: Shape
kernel.statement: A point, area or volume in a declared coordinate system; any coordinate resolves to every node that contains it.
kernel.note: any declared coordinate system; point, box (across a wrapping seam), ball and polygon; containment scans every shape in a system (no spatial index yet) and polygons are planar on the first two axes

kernel.name: Attributes
kernel.statement: Typed values declared in the registry; text is multilingual through Expression, sensitive values are encrypted through Security.
kernel.note: typed and encrypted when sensitive; multilingual text waits for Expression (P12)

kernel.name: Versions
kernel.statement: Bi-temporal history: valid time and recorded time; nothing is overwritten and any past state can be queried.

kernel.name: Events
kernel.statement: One event log that every change and declared occurrence is written to; workflows, notifications, analytics, webhooks and audit read it.
kernel.note: the kernel's log is hash-chained; audit_log and the webhook bus (lib/events.js) are not yet merged into it (GAP-27)

kernel.name: Change Lifecycle
kernel.statement: Draft, validate, preview, approve, publish (now or scheduled), roll back; hide is reversible; delete is archive, then purge with a separate permission.
kernel.note: changes are drafted as data and validated, previewed, approved (with the approve permission, by someone other than the author), published now or on schedule and rolled back; nodes hide (left out of every listing), archive and purge with a separate permission. Purge cannot remove codes already written in earlier event payloads, because the log is never edited

kernel.name: Views
kernel.statement: A platform, tenant, module or subscriber selects hierarchies, subtrees, depth, groupings and labels by reference, never by copy.
kernel.note: subtrees by root, depth and kind, with labels, by reference and computed live; groupings are not yet declarable

kernel.name: Scope
kernel.statement: Every declaration lives in a namespace (platform, tenant, publisher) and at a scope level (platform, tenant, store, channel, place, language, segment, device type, person).
kernel.note: a value is assigned in a namespace at any scope node (the scope levels are kinds); kinds, hierarchies and views are scoped by namespace only

kernel.name: Resolution
kernel.statement: One resolver answers what applies here and now from relationships, hierarchies (nearest wins), time windows, context and rules; settings and defaults are its answers, not stored copies.
kernel.note: one resolver: nearest assignment up each hierarchy, profiles order hierarchies, namespaces most specific first, the answer says where it came from; time windows apply, rules (Rule) are not yet an input

buildStatuses.means: declared and contracted, with no code and no live route yet; its contract's APIs are designed interfaces
owns code or live routes, but not everything its contract describes
everything its contract describes runs, and its laws are enforced

amendments.summary: Unifies the registry under one categorised ownership spine: 13 categories; every domain in exactly one category; every primitive and term owned by exactly one domain (ownership stated only here); the four undeclared owners resolved (Constitutional Authority and Runtime declared as domains, Perspective and Possibility declared, Existence owned by Identity); new domains for the platform; every artifact owned by one domain.
changes: domains.json: categories, category per domain, 28 domains added, owns completed
primitives.json: owner field removed (ownership is declared once, in domains.json)
terminology.json: ownerDomain removed; terms added for newly owned names

amendments.summary: Writes the 17 missing domain contracts (Decision, Geo, Time, Measure, Value, Expression, Registry, Compliance, Experience, Communication, Notification, Guidance, Integration, Insight, Content, Offering, Package) into the registry, replacing FOUNDATIONS.md as their source; documents are filed by the owning domain's register category, so the manifest's separate document categories are retired.
changes: manifest.json: 17 artifacts; categories, totalArtifacts and per-artifact cat removed

amendments.summary: One master document: the registry projects UCOS-MASTER.md and one volume per register category, replacing the per-artifact files and the repository index; the enforced laws become registry data.
changes: audit.js: checks the master and volumes

amendments.summary: FOUNDATIONS.md absorbed: one law register (26 laws merging the corpus's laws and principles and the foundation rules, each with sources and enforcement status), the kernel parts K01–K12 with one owner each, the Party domain and its contract, the code-module map (codebase.json), and the build path with its decisions (roadmap.json). FOUNDATIONS.md moves to _superseded.

The concept register: every corpus concept placed once. Kind rules and owner rules in classification.json (owned by Semantic); every concept-holding container (5,609) and every concept in a structural container (3,552) reviewed by agents with independent second opinions on low-confidence calls and a maintainer sample check; the register is derived at compile time, sealed, gated and searchable by owner and category; low-confidence decisions form the master's review queue.
changes: project.js: concept register chapter and review queue

amendments.summary: One set of domains: the other structures that call their parts domains are aligned to the register. GOIP's 67 incentive domains and the 7 capability domains each name their one register owner (alignment.json); every per-universe record engine takes its reviewed container's owner; the capability-domain list moves from lib/registry.js into seed data.
changes: lib/ucos-domain.js: owner and category per universe

amendments.summary: Every document has one registered status and owner (documents.json). 18 hand-written documents that the user manual, the master or the registry now cover — topic guides, flow diagrams, implementation summaries, an old code review and two roadmaps — move to _superseded with what replaced each. The compiler's corpus inputs are derived from the parser's document list, which puts the UCRS constitution in the seal's manifest for the first time.

The registry tells the truth about what runs. The live API (lib/api.js, 725 routes) is registered with one owning domain per route (api.json); every domain carries a build status derived from what it owns (designed: no code and no routes); mixed modules in the code map are split so storage, links, places and value units sit with their owners; the 25 gaps the audit found are recorded with owners and status (roadmap.json → gaps). Test isolation: tests may no longer open the default database.
changes: codebase.json: registry.js, global.js, db.js split; storage adapters to Persistence

amendments.summary: The kernel's first slice runs (P08 in progress). lib/kernel.js holds kinds and typed attributes (K01, K06), nodes with universal IDs and identifier schemes in time windows (K02, K04), named hierarchies of any depth where one node may sit in many places (K03), bi-temporal versions where nothing is overwritten (K07) and one hash-chained event log that is the recorded time of every other table (K08). The kernel names no domain vocabulary; its namespaces, value types and event names are data (lib/seed/kernel.json). Each kernel part now carries a build status. The development server runs from the repository's new location (GAP-21 closed); the coexisting event records are recorded as GAP-27 and a one-off smoke-test connection reset as GAP-28.
changes: domains.json: kernel part status; LAW-020 and LAW-024 enforcement
roadmap.json: P08 in progress; GAP-06 retitled; GAP-21 closed; GAP-27, GAP-28
project.js: kernel status in the master

amendments.summary: The kernel's read side runs. Shape (K05, lib/kernel-shape.js): coordinate systems are data (axes, bounds, wrapping), shapes have valid time, and any coordinate resolves to every node that contains it, from a site to a galaxy. Scope and resolution (K11, K12, lib/kernel-context.js): a setting is declared once, assigned in a namespace at any scope node, and one resolver answers what applies here and now — nearest wins, profiles order hierarchies, every answer says where it came from, and nothing assigned stays unresolved. Views (K10): subtrees selected by reference and computed live. Namespaces carry their holder (tenant:42); kinds and hierarchies not declared in a namespace are the platform's. CI could not run on 3e67d62 because the GitHub account's billing blocked the jobs (GAP-29).
changes: lib/kernel.js: namespace holders; platform fallback for kinds and hierarchies; shared internals
domains.json: K05, K10, K11, K12 partial; Perspective partial (owns views)

amendments.summary: The kernel's change lifecycle runs (K09, lib/kernel-lifecycle.js). A change is a list of kernel operations written as data; it is validated and previewed by dry runs that leave nothing behind, approved by someone other than its author, published now or at a scheduled time, and rolled back by closing what it recorded and reopening what it superseded — refused while a later change still builds on it. A node hides (reversibly), archives, and is purged only when archived and only with the separate purge permission, leaving a tombstone event. States, transitions, operations and the permission are data (lib/seed/kernel.json → lifecycle). Every kernel part now runs; none is fully built.

Kernel follow-ups. Hidden and archived nodes drop out of every kernel listing — node lists, children, subtrees, views and coordinate lookups — unless a caller asks for them; paths, ancestors and history keep the whole structure, and hiding a node does not hide what sits under it. Approving a change needs the declared approve permission, which the caller is granted by Authority; the kernel checks grants, never role names. Node states moved into the kernel's own tables.
changes: lib/kernel-shape.js, lib/kernel-context.js: listings leave out hidden nodes

amendments.summary: P09 begins: places are on the kernel. Every country and subdivision is a node of the place kind (declared as data in lib/seed/places.json) in one place tree — countries at the top, nothing invented above them, subdivisions under their country or parent subdivision to any depth — with its code as an identifier in its declared scheme and its row's universal ID as its own. lib/places.js mirrors the master after every write and on every boot: a rename is a new version, a switched-off country is hidden, a re-parented subdivision moves with its past kept, a deleted row is archived; a warm pass writes nothing. The tables remain the source until the writes move onto the kernel.
changes: lib/kernel.js: createNode adopts an existing universal ID; placementsOf; writes take the lock up front
lib/registry.js reconcileDerived, lib/entity.js propagate, lib/global.js country writes: mirror the place tree

amendments.summary: A place's currency and locale are no longer facts of the place. They are settings owned by Value and Expression (declared in lib/seed/places.json), assigned at the place's node on the kernel and answered by the resolver — so a subdivision inherits its country's currency, and a setting assigned at a subdivision applies there and below. registry.country(), through which the platform's readers ask, answers currency and locale from the kernel and a country's money symbol and decimals from its currency in Value's master; a country profile's tax is the tax engine's rule, no longer the country's legacy tax columns. The master's columns remain as the mirror's input until the writes move onto the kernel.
changes: lib/places.js: settings declared and assigned; facts()
lib/registry.js: country(), countries() and countryProfile() read the kernel, the currency master and the tax engine
